subject: problems in examples having multivariate distribution

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: problems in examples having multivariate distribution
parts:
As promised, this is reporting results about examples
involving multivariate dsn.

In Bugs example vol2:

birats is another model for the notorious rats data, which has
specification of inv_wishart and multi_normal. Now the cpp
code is not able to be complied at least for reasons of no
matching multi_normal_log function and some others.
(I hope that my clang++/g++ on Linux did not confound
this issue as I often could not make examples that worked
before work.)

eyes and stagnant are two examples, which has multivariate
dsn and discrete dsn. I am not able to compile them. Are we
not supporting discrete dsn yet?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] problems in examples having multivariate distribution
parts:
We don't have discrete parameter sampling working yet
for the models. Discrete data's OK.

The multivariate densities need to be translated from
direct calls to Eigen to our own matrix wrappers, which
promote floating point to auto-dif matrix variables.

Daniel's working on the distributions and Matt's
working on the discrete sampling. (I've now turned
to the R integration.)

- Bob
